rationale: Most common KpSC carbapenemase. Other blaKPC variants (blaKPC-3, -4, …) share >99% nt identity but are not in our current reference.
CTX-M ESBL family. Group-1 (CTX-M-15, -65, -27) and group-9 (CTX-M-14) cross-map heavily at the gene CDS. Aggregating matches clinical reporting ("blaCTX-M present").
NDM metallo-β-lactamases. NDM-1 vs NDM-5 differ at 2 amino acids (6 nt) — reads multi-map across both CDS positions.
OXA-48-like carbapenemases. OXA-48 vs OXA-181 differ at 4 amino acids — same multi-mapping behaviour. OXA-232 added (Phase E) — OXA-48-like variant, same multi-mapping.
Standalone — no significant paralog in the current reference panel.

Trimethoprim DHFR (Phase E). dfrA12 vs dfrA14 ~60-70% nt identity — distinct, no heavy cross-mapping; kept separate.
Sulfonamide DHPS (Phase E). sul1 vs sul2 ~50% identity — distinct genes, not allele variants; kept separate.
Aminoglycoside 3-N-acetyltransferase IIa (Phase E). Standalone — distinct from aac6-Ib-cr.
